info.name: Kilivana Backend API
info.description:
Every endpoint that currently exists in the Kilivana Spring Boot backend (verified against the running OpenAPI document at /api-docs).

1. Import this file into Postman.
2. Open "1. Authentication" and send "Login (ADMIN)" (or the role you need).
3. Every other request already carries Authorization: Bearer <token> and full URLs, so just press Send.

Each request description shows the path pattern (for example /api/v1/products/{id}) and the concrete id it currently uses, so you know what to replace.

To test through the ngrok tunnel, replace http://localhost:8080 with https://either-juvenile-progeny.ngrok-free.dev in the URLs.

Responses use the envelope: { "success", "message", "data", "timestamp", "error" }.

18. Image Storage
item.description: StoredImageController. Image bytes live in PostgreSQL when app.storage.provider=database, or when the Cloudinary fallback kicked in. Reads are public because image URLs are embedded in tags and mobile payloads that cannot send a bearer token.

request.description: Returns the raw bytes for a stored image id with its original content type. Replace 1 with the publicId from an upload response.
